origin_faqs.question: Which body regulates nurses in Uganda and issues the good-standing document?
origin_faqs.answer: The Uganda Nurses and Midwives Council (UNMC) is the statutory regulator. It registers/enrols nurses and midwives, issues the annual practising licence, and issues the Certificate of Good Standing (also called a Verification of Registration/Letter of Good Standing) that foreign regulators such as the UK NMC, Ireland's NMBI and AHPRA in Australia require.

origin_faqs.question: How do I get a Certificate of Good Standing from UNMC?
origin_faqs.answer: Apply to UNMC (in person at their offices or via their online portal/email) with your registration/enrolment number, a valid current practising licence, your certificates, ID/passport and the prescribed fee. UNMC then confirms your registration status and produces the good-standing letter. Because you must hold a current UNMC licence to be in good standing, renew any lapsed practising licence first. Confirm the exact current fee and forms directly with UNMC as these change.

origin_faqs.question: Does UNMC send the verification directly to the foreign regulator, or to me?
origin_faqs.answer: Most overseas regulators (NMC UK, NMBI Ireland, AHPRA) require the verification to come directly from the source regulator, often through their own online verification request. UNMC can respond to these regulator-to-regulator verifications, and can also issue you a sealed/stamped letter. Check the destination regulator's process (many now use an online portal like NMC's or CGFNS/verification services) and ask UNMC to send it directly where required rather than handing you the only copy.

origin_faqs.question: Do my Ugandan documents need a Hague apostille or embassy legalisation?
origin_faqs.answer: Do not assume an apostille alone will be accepted. The usual Ugandan route is authentication by the issuing institution, then the Ministry of Education and Sports (for academic/professional certificates), then the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and finally legalisation at the destination country's embassy/high commission. Uganda's status under the Hague Apostille Convention has been complicated by objections from some member states, so apostille may not be recognised by every country. Confirm the exact chain with the destination embassy and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs before paying for anything.

origin_faqs.question: Is OET required, or does UNMC have its own English rule?
origin_faqs.answer: Nursing in Uganda is taught and practised in English, but UNMC does not sit your English test for going abroad — the destination regulator sets the English requirement. The UK NMC, NMBI (Ireland) and AHPRA (Australia) accept OET (Occupational English Test) at the required grade (typically Grade B / around CEFR C1 in the relevant sub-tests), or IELTS Academic as an alternative. So you take OET/IELTS for the foreign regulator, separate from any UNMC documentation.

origin_faqs.question: Can I sit OET in Uganda?
origin_faqs.answer: OET is delivered by computer-based testing and remotely-proctored options, and test sittings are accessible from Uganda; you register and pay through the official OET website and pick an available centre or remote-proctored slot. Availability of a physical Kampala venue can change, so check the OET site for current test locations and dates when you book.

origin_faqs.question: How long does the UNMC good-standing/verification take?
origin_faqs.answer: Processing time varies with your file being complete, your licence being current, and UNMC's workload, so a fixed number cannot be promised. Apply well ahead of any deadline, make sure your practising licence is renewed first, and follow up directly with UNMC for their current turnaround rather than relying on a quoted figure.

origin_faqs.question: What is the overall path from Uganda to working as a nurse in the UK, Ireland or Australia?
origin_faqs.answer: Broadly: hold a current UNMC registration and licence; sit OET (or IELTS) at the required level; open an account with the destination regulator (NMC UK, NMBI Ireland, or AHPRA/Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia); request UNMC good-standing/verification to that regulator; pass any required knowledge test and clinical/competency assessment (for the UK, the CBT and OSCE that make up the Test of Competence; Ireland and Australia have their own assessment/decision routes); then obtain a job offer and work visa. Requirements differ by country, so follow each regulator's official checklist.

origin_faqs.question: Do I need to keep renewing my Uganda licence while I am abroad?
origin_faqs.answer: If you may need further verifications later or intend to keep your UNMC registration active, you generally must keep renewing your Ugandan practising licence, otherwise your registration can lapse and a future good-standing letter becomes harder to obtain. Confirm UNMC's renewal rules and any grace period with the Council directly.

uk_faqs.question: As a Ugandan-trained registered nurse, how does my good-standing reach the NMC?
uk_faqs.answer: The NMC requires proof of registration and good standing directly from every regulator you have been registered with. For you that is the Uganda Nurses and Midwives Council (UNMC). The NMC sends UNMC a verification/reference form and UNMC returns it board-to-board (regulator-to-regulator), rather than you uploading it yourself. Request this from UNMC early, as African councils can be slow to respond. If UNMC has been registered less than the required look-back period, confirm the exact form with the NMC.

uk_faqs.question: What English test must I pass, given English is an official language in Uganda?
uk_faqs.answer: Even though English is Uganda's official language and language of nurse training, the NMC still requires evidence. Most Ugandan applicants sit OET (Nursing) needing at least B in Reading, Listening and Speaking and C+ in Writing, or IELTS Academic 7.0 overall (7.0 in reading/listening/speaking, 6.5 writing). A Ugandan nursing qualification alone does not exempt you; however, you may instead qualify via a recent qualification taught and examined in English or recent practice in a majority-English country - confirm your eligibility route with the NMC.

uk_faqs.question: What is the NMC assessment process I must complete?
uk_faqs.answer: After the qualification and English checks, you sit the Test of Competence: a computer-based test (CBT) with a clinical and a professional part, which you can take in a test centre (including options accessible from Uganda/online where permitted), followed by the OSCE (Objective Structured Clinical Examination), which is a practical exam taken in person in the UK. You normally start the OSCE after arriving and being sponsored by a UK employer.

uk_faqs.question: Do my Ugandan documents (diploma, transcripts, good-standing) need an apostille for the NMC?
uk_faqs.answer: The NMC verifies your qualification through your training institution and UNMC rather than requiring apostille legalisation for registration. Uganda acceded to the Hague Apostille Convention (in force from 2025), so where any UK body does ask for legalised documents you can now obtain an apostille from Uganda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs instead of full embassy legalisation. Confirm current document requirements directly with the NMC and your UK employer.

uk_faqs.question: In what currency do I pay NMC fees from Uganda?
uk_faqs.answer: NMC fees are charged in British pounds (GBP) and paid online by card, not in Ugandan shillings (UGX). Your bank will convert UGX to GBP at the prevailing rate plus any card/forex charges. Budget separately for the CBT fee, the OSCE fee, the NMC application and registration fees, plus your OET/IELTS and visa costs.

uk_faqs.question: Which UK visa lets me come and work as a nurse from Uganda?
uk_faqs.answer: The Health and Care Worker visa (a route within the Skilled Worker system) is designed for nurses. You need a UK employer that is a licensed sponsor to issue a Certificate of Sponsorship for an eligible nursing role. Many Ugandan nurses are recruited into a pre-registration band and sit the OSCE after arrival. You will also complete a TB test at an approved clinic before applying, as Uganda is a listed country for UK TB testing.

uk_faqs.question: Can I start working before I finish the OSCE and get on the NMC register?
uk_faqs.answer: Typically yes in a temporary capacity: many UK employers sponsor Ugandan nurses as pre-registration nurses or healthcare assistants while you complete the OSCE, then move you to registered-nurse pay once the NMC adds you to the register. This is arranged with your sponsoring employer; confirm the exact interim role and pay with them.

origin_faqs.question: Which body regulates nurses in South Africa and issues the good-standing document?
origin_faqs.answer: The South African Nursing Council (SANC) is the statutory regulator. It issues a Verification of Registration and Status (often called a Certificate of Good Standing), which overseas regulators such as the UK NMC, Ireland's NMBI and AHPRA in Australia require to confirm you are registered and have no disciplinary findings against you.

origin_faqs.question: How do I request the good-standing / verification certificate from SANC?
origin_faqs.answer: You apply to SANC for a 'Verification of Registration and Status'. You submit the request with your details and the prescribed fee, and specify the overseas council it must go to. It is advisable to apply directly through SANC and confirm the current form, fee and turnaround on the SANC website, as processes and fees change.

origin_faqs.question: Does SANC send the verification directly to the overseas regulator?
origin_faqs.answer: Yes — overseas councils like the NMC, NMBI and AHPRA generally require the verification to be sent directly from SANC to them (regulator-to-regulator), not handed to you. When you apply, state the destination council so SANC can send it directly. Confirm the exact delivery method with both SANC and the receiving council.

origin_faqs.question: How long does the SANC verification take?
origin_faqs.answer: Turnaround varies and SANC has at times had significant backlogs. There is no single guaranteed timeframe, so apply as early as possible and confirm the current processing time directly with SANC rather than relying on a fixed number.

origin_faqs.question: Do my South African documents need an apostille or embassy legalisation?
origin_faqs.answer: South Africa is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so South African public documents (e.g. qualifications, police clearance) are authenticated with an apostille rather than full embassy legalisation for use in other Convention countries. Apostilles are issued by DIRCO (the Department of International Relations and Cooperation) or by the High Court for certain documents. The UK, Ireland and Australia are also Convention members, so an apostille — not consular legalisation — is normally what applies.

origin_faqs.question: Do I need the OET, or does my English count because I trained in South Africa?
origin_faqs.answer: This depends on the destination regulator, not SANC. The NMC, NMBI and AHPRA all accept OET (usually grade B, with some flexibility) or IELTS as evidence of English. Some allow an exemption if your entire nursing programme was taught and assessed in English and you meet their criteria. Check each regulator's current English-language policy, as recognised-country and exemption rules differ.

origin_faqs.question: Is the OET different from any English requirement of SANC?
origin_faqs.answer: SANC does not require the OET — the OET is an overseas requirement. SANC's role is to confirm your South African registration and good standing. The OET (or IELTS) is set by the receiving country's regulator (NMC/NMBI/AHPRA) as their language proof, so you deal with those bodies for the test, not with SANC.

origin_faqs.question: What English score do UK, Ireland and Australia typically want on the OET?
origin_faqs.answer: They commonly accept OET grade B in each of the four sub-tests (listening, reading, writing, speaking), and several now allow combining scores across two sittings or accept a C+ in writing under conditions. Because these thresholds are periodically updated, verify the exact current requirement on the NMC, NMBI or AHPRA website before booking.

origin_faqs.question: What overseas registration route follows the good-standing certificate?
origin_faqs.answer: After SANC verification and English proof, the UK route is NMC registration including the CBT and OSCE; Ireland is NMBI which may require a qualification assessment and possibly adaptation/aptitude testing; Australia is AHPRA/NMBA via the outcomes-based assessment (a portfolio/MCQ plus OSCE) unless you qualify for another stream. Confirm the current steps directly with each regulator.

uk_faqs.question: Which South African body confirms my registration, and how does it reach the NMC?
uk_faqs.answer: Your regulator is the South African Nursing Council (SANC). The NMC requires verification of registration from every regulator you have been registered with. SANC issues a Certificate of Status / Verification of Registration; the NMC prefers this to come directly from the regulator rather than from your own hands. Because arrangements change, confirm with the NMC and SANC exactly whether SANC sends it board-to-board electronically or by sealed post to the NMC.

uk_faqs.question: What English test does the NMC accept for a South African nurse?
uk_faqs.answer: Even though English is an official language of South Africa, the NMC still requires evidence. You can sit OET (Nursing) needing at least B in Writing and grade C+ in the other components (Reading, Listening, Speaking), or IELTS Academic 7.0. The NMC may also accept employer/education-based English evidence in some routes, so confirm with the NMC which applies to you.

uk_faqs.question: Do I need an apostille or embassy legalisation on my South African documents for the NMC?
uk_faqs.answer: South Africa is a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so where a document needs authentication it is apostilled (through DIRCO or a High Court), not legalised at a UK embassy. However, the NMC application itself does not generally require apostilled documents — that step is more often for your visa or employer. Confirm with the NMC what certification level it wants on each document.

uk_faqs.question: What is the CBT and OSCE, and where do I do them?
uk_faqs.answer: The NMC uses a two-part Test of Competence: the CBT (computer-based test) which you can sit at a Pearson VUE centre, including in South Africa, and the OSCE (practical exam) which must be taken at an approved test centre in the UK, usually after you arrive and start work. Confirm current CBT availability in South Africa with the NMC/Pearson VUE.

uk_faqs.question: In what currency do I pay the NMC fees?
uk_faqs.answer: NMC fees are charged in British pounds (GBP), so from South Africa you pay by card and your bank converts from South African rand (ZAR), adding exchange and card fees. Budget for the CBT, OSCE, the NMC registration fee and the separate ongoing annual retention fee, all in GBP.

uk_faqs.question: Which visa do I use to work as a nurse in the UK?
uk_faqs.answer: Nursing is eligible for the Health and Care Worker visa (a Skilled Worker route), which requires a Certificate of Sponsorship from an approved UK employer. Nurses are exempt from the Immigration Health Surcharge on this visa. You will need to show your English evidence and, for the visa, a police clearance and possibly a TB test certificate — confirm current requirements with UKVI.

uk_faqs.question: Do I need a South African police clearance and TB test?
uk_faqs.answer: For the Health and Care Worker visa, applicants who have lived in South Africa are required to provide a South African Police Service (SAPS) police clearance certificate, and South Africa is on the UK's TB-testing list, so you will need a TB test from a UKVI-approved clinic. Confirm the exact document list with UKVI before you apply.

uk_faqs.question: Roughly how long does the whole NMC process take?
uk_faqs.answer: Timelines vary, but obtaining SANC verification, passing the CBT, getting an NMC decision, securing a sponsor and visa, then sitting the OSCE in the UK commonly spans several months to a year. Because SANC turnaround and NMC processing times change, confirm current estimates with both regulators.

origin_faqs.question: Who is the nursing regulator in Cameroon and who issues my Certificate of Good Standing / verification?
origin_faqs.answer: Cameroon created the Ordre National des Infirmiers, Infirmières et Sages-Femmes du Cameroun (the national nursing and midwifery order) by law, but for many years registration and professional verification have in practice been handled through the Ministry of Public Health (MINSANTE) and its regional delegations. Depending on when and where you trained, your good-standing letter, attestation d'exercice, and registration confirmation may come from the Ordre, from MINSANTE, or from your training school. Confirm directly with the Ordre / MINSANTE which body issues your verification, because foreign regulators (NMC, AHPRA, NMBI) require it to come from an official authority.

origin_faqs.question: Does the UK NMC / Australia AHPRA / Ireland NMBI require verification sent directly by Cameroon's authority?
origin_faqs.answer: Yes — these regulators generally require your registration and good-standing to be verified by the issuing authority itself, not just a copy you hold. Whether Cameroon's Ordre or MINSANTE will send it directly to the foreign regulator is something you must confirm, as processes here are not always standardised. If the authority cannot send it directly, ask the foreign regulator (NMC/AHPRA/NMBI) what alternative proof of authenticity they will accept. Do not assume a fixed process — confirm with both sides in writing.

origin_faqs.question: Do my Cameroon documents need an apostille?
origin_faqs.answer: No. Cameroon is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention, so an apostille is not available for Cameroonian documents. Instead you must use embassy/consular legalisation: documents are typically authenticated by the relevant Cameroonian authorities and the Ministry of External Relations (MINREX), then legalised by the embassy or consulate of the destination country (UK, Australia or Ireland). Always check the current requirement with the destination country's embassy, as some regulators accept certified translations instead of full legalisation.

origin_faqs.question: What is the document legalisation chain for a Cameroonian nurse?
origin_faqs.answer: The usual path is: (1) obtain original/certified documents (diploma, transcripts, good-standing/attestation); (2) have them authenticated by the issuing institution and MINSANTE where required; (3) legalise through MINREX (Ministry of External Relations); (4) present to the destination country's embassy for consular legalisation if they require it. Because Cameroon has no apostille, this multi-step legalisation replaces it. Confirm the exact steps with MINREX and the embassy before paying any fees.

origin_faqs.question: Can I meet the English requirement without OET, given I trained in English?
origin_faqs.answer: Possibly. The NMC, AHPRA and NMBI accept OET (Occupational English Test) at the required grade (usually B in each sub-test, with some flexibility). They may also accept IELTS Academic. If you trained and practised in English, some regulators allow an English-language exemption based on your education and recent employment being conducted in English — but this is decided by the foreign regulator, not by Cameroon's council. Anglophone Cameroonian nurses should check whether they qualify for an exemption before paying for OET.

origin_faqs.question: OET or the council's own English rule — which one matters?
origin_faqs.answer: For working abroad, the destination regulator's English rule is what counts. Cameroon's Ordre/MINSANTE does not set the English standard for the UK, Australia or Ireland — the NMC, AHPRA and NMBI do. So plan around OET (or IELTS/exemption) requirements of the country you are going to, not any local language rule.

origin_faqs.question: How long does it take to get my good-standing / verification from Cameroon?
origin_faqs.answer: There is no reliable published turnaround, and in practice it can vary widely depending on the office and region. Do not rely on a fixed number — request it as early as possible, keep copies of every submission and receipt, and follow up in person or through your training school. Confirm the expected timeframe directly with the Ordre / MINSANTE office handling your file.

origin_faqs.question: My documents are in French — do I need translations?
origin_faqs.answer: Yes, for the UK (NMC), Australia (AHPRA) and Ireland (NMBI) any French-language documents generally need certified English translations. Use a translator the foreign regulator accepts, and keep the original French plus the translation together. Anglophone-system Cameroonian documents already in English usually do not need translation, but transcripts and stamps in French still may.

origin_faqs.question: What is the overall route for a Cameroonian nurse to work in the UK, Australia or Ireland?
origin_faqs.answer: In broad terms: (1) confirm your registration/good-standing source in Cameroon (Ordre or MINSANTE) and request verification; (2) meet the English requirement via OET, IELTS, or an exemption; (3) create your account and application with the destination regulator (NMC, AHPRA or NMBI) and pass their competence/qualification assessment (e.g. NMC CBT and OSCE); (4) legalise/translate your Cameroonian documents (embassy legalisation, not apostille); (5) secure a job offer and the relevant work visa (e.g. UK Health and Care Worker visa). Verify each regulator's current steps and fees on their official website, as they change.

uk_faqs.question: As a Cameroon-registered nurse, how does my proof of good standing reach the NMC?
uk_faqs.answer: The NMC requires a board-to-board confirmation of registration sent directly from your regulator. In Cameroon that is the Ordre National des Infirmiers, Infirmieres et Infirmiers-Anesthesistes du Cameroun (ONIIAC), with registration ultimately under the Ministry of Public Health. You request the confirmation from them and it should be sent directly to the NMC rather than uploaded by you. If ONIIAC is unfamiliar with the NMC board-to-board form, confirm the exact routing with the NMC before applying.

uk_faqs.question: Does Cameroon issue an apostille for my NMC documents, or do I need embassy legalisation?
uk_faqs.answer: Cameroon is not a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, so an apostille is not available. Documents such as your qualification certificate or good-standing letter that need legalisation must go through embassy/consular legalisation (Ministry of External Relations plus the relevant embassy) rather than apostille. For the NMC application specifically, most verification is done board-to-board, so confirm with the NMC which of your documents actually require legalisation before paying for it.

uk_faqs.question: My nursing diploma from Cameroon is in French. Do I need it translated for the NMC?
uk_faqs.answer: Yes. Cameroon is bilingual, but if your qualification, transcript or good-standing document is issued in French you must provide a certified English translation alongside the original. The NMC requires translations by an approved/certified translator. Documents already issued in English (common in Anglophone regions and English-medium schools) do not need translating.

uk_faqs.question: What English test do I take for the NMC as a nurse from Cameroon?
uk_faqs.answer: Cameroon is not on the NMC's list of majority-English-speaking countries, so you must evidence English. The accepted route for nurses is OET at grade B in Reading, Listening and Speaking, and at least grade C+ in Writing (the NMC allows the C+ concession in Writing). IELTS Academic 7.0 overall is the alternative. You may combine two sittings within six months if each meets the minimum. Confirm current score rules with the NMC as they update periodically.

uk_faqs.question: What are the NMC's clinical exams and where do I sit them from Cameroon?
uk_faqs.answer: The NMC uses a two-part Test of Competence: the CBT (computer-based test), which you can sit online/at a Pearson VUE centre from Cameroon or the region, and the OSCE (objective structured clinical examination), which is taken in person at an approved test centre in the UK after you arrive. You typically pass the CBT before travelling and complete the OSCE within a set window once employed.

uk_faqs.question: Which UK visa do I use, and can my Cameroon employer/sponsor arrange it?
uk_faqs.answer: Nurses use the Health and Care Worker visa (a Skilled Worker route for eligible health roles). You need a Certificate of Sponsorship from a UK employer with a sponsor licence. The role must meet the salary and skill thresholds. As a Cameroonian national you will also complete tuberculosis testing at an approved clinic before the visa, since Cameroon is on the UK's TB-test list.

uk_faqs.question: In what currency do I pay NMC and visa fees from Cameroon?
uk_faqs.answer: The NMC charges in pounds sterling (GBP) and payment is by card, so your Central African CFA franc (XAF) account is converted at your bank's card rate plus any foreign-exchange fee. Visa fees and the Immigration Health Surcharge are also in GBP. Budget for exchange-rate movement between the XAF and GBP when planning your total costs.

uk_faqs.question: Roughly what is the order of steps for a Cameroon nurse joining the NMC register?
uk_faqs.answer: Create an NMC online account and self-assessment, sit OET/IELTS to the required grades, pass the CBT, arrange the board-to-board good-standing confirmation from ONIIAC/Ministry of Public Health, submit your qualification and identity evidence (with certified English translations if in French), receive a decision, then travel on a Health and Care Worker visa and complete the OSCE in the UK before final registration. Confirm current sequencing with the NMC as steps can be updated.
